name: Bode's Galaxy, the Cigar Galaxy and the integrated flux nebulae
subtitle: Single-image broadband with hydrogen, HaLRGB

facts.Optique: SharpStar 94EDPH refractor (94 mm aperture) with its dedicated reducer, 409 mm focal length (f/4.4)
facts.Caméra: QHY268M (monochrome), gain 56, offset 25, High Gain 2CMS mode, cooled to −15 °C (0 °C for the Ha), 1×1 binning

sections.title: Description
sections.html:
This 3.3° by 2.2° field, in Ursa Major, shows the most famous pair of galaxies in the northern sky, about 12 million light-years away.

M81, Bode's Galaxy, is the large spiral seen at three-quarter view, left of centre: a yellow core of old stars, surrounded by bluish arms where young stars are forming. Above it, M82, the Cigar Galaxy, is seen edge-on. A close encounter with M81 triggered a burst of star formation there, whose wind blows large jets of red hydrogen out on either side of the disc; these are what the Ha filter brings out. At lower left, the small galaxy NGC 3077 belongs to the same group.

The whole field is crossed by very faint grey-brown veils: these are the integrated flux nebulae, dust from our own Galaxy lying well above its plane and lit only by the overall light of the Milky Way. They are in the foreground, thousands of times closer than the galaxies. Seeing them takes a very dark sky and a long integration time.

The colours are close to the real ones: they were calibrated on the stars in the field, and the hydrogen only strengthens the red.

This image was acquired in collaboration with Renaud Venne-Landry.

sections.html:
Location
Starfront remote site, Texas (31°32'51" N, 99°22'55" W)
Period
10 October 2025 to 14 March 2026
Camera
QHY268M (monochrome), gain 56, offset 25, High Gain 2CMS mode, cooled to −15 °C (0 °C for the Ha), 1×1 binning
Optics
SharpStar 94EDPH refractor (94 mm aperture) with its dedicated reducer, 409 mm focal length (f/4.4)

1.90"/pixel (3.76 µm pixels)
Filters
L, R, G, B and Ha
Software
Voyager (RoboTarget)

32.2 h in LRGB + 16.2 h in Ha = 48.3 h (483 frames). Two of the 99 Ha frames could not be aligned and were discarded.

sections.title: Processing
sections.html:
Done entirely in PixInsight 1.9.6, starting from the raw frames.

Preprocessing (per filter)

  • Calibration: 300 s master darks at −15 °C (LRGB) and 600 s at 0 °C (Ha); L, R, G, B master flats at −15 °C from December 2025; Ha master flat from October 2025.
  • Frame alignment, local normalization, stacking.
  • Astrometric solution of each stack.

Preparation

  • RGB combination and colour calibration on the stars in the field (BackgroundNeutralization then ColorCalibration, white taken on the stars in the field).
  • Common cropping of the edges.

Linear processing

  • Light gradient correction (AutomaticBackgroundExtractor, degree-1 polynomial, so as not to erase the faint dust in the field).
  • BlurXTerminator (deconvolution), NoiseXTerminator (noise reduction), StarXTerminator (separation of stars and nebulae), on the colour, the luminance and the Ha.

Non-linear processing

  • Background neutralization, then linked stretch of the three colours, target background level 0.20.
  • Injection of the Ha into the red (40%) and into the luminance.
  • Colour saturation boosted in the galaxies only (lightness mask), before the combination with the luminance, which would otherwise wash it out.
  • Combination of the luminance with the colour (LRGB).
  • Compression of the galaxy cores: HDRMultiscaleTransform in two passes (6 layers then 4 layers), with a lightness mask, to reveal the spiral right down to the core of M81 and the dust lanes at the centre of M82.
  • Saturation raised a second time in the bright areas.
  • Green toned down (SCNR 0.7), contrast and saturation curves.
  • Reintegration of the stars, stretched less than the nebulae.

Notes

  • Tenth version of the rendering: the earlier ones showed grey galaxies. The arms of M81 keep a salmon tint, pinker than the expected blue; the background dust is unchanged.
  • DarkStructureEnhance was not applied: on a first rendering, it carved an artificial dark halo around M81.
  • The integrated flux nebulae are heavily stretched; their tint depends strongly on the background neutralization.
  • Colours calibrated with ColorCalibration rather than SPCC, which gave too orange a rendering.
  • Final adjustments made by hand in PixInsight.
